state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Interesting. Can you explain why you think the arrow on the number line must start at zero? Let's think about what the starting point of the arrow represents in relation to the values on the number line.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I thought the arrow always starts at zero because that's where we usually start counting. But now that you mention it, I see that the arrow starts at -12 in this case. So, if I follow the +10 from -12, I’m not really sure how to figure out where that goes. Can you help me understand how to find the end point of that arrow?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: That's a great observation about the starting point of the arrow. Since the arrow starts at -12, think about how moving to the right by +10 affects the position on the number line. Can you describe what happens when you add +10 to -12 in terms of direction and value?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly names and addresses the zero-starting misconception in Turn 1, maintains high cognitive demand by asking the student to reason about position and movement, and the student demonstrates clear progress by recognizing the arrow starts at -12 and seeking to understand how to work with that starting point.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never directly provides the answer, and helps the student discover their misconception about the starting point through questioning rather than telling.
